segments: The Fourth Discourse.
The Kings of the Chaldeans.
who, in his might, burned the Temple and the city,
and took Zedekiah captive and blinded his eyes,
and carried all the Jews into exile,
except for the poor.
And the kingdom of Judah ceased, which had survived after the cessation of the kingdom of the children of Israel for one hundred and fifty-five years.
Now Jeremiah, when he knew of the burning of the Temple, hid in a cave the Tabernacle of the Testimony and the Ark,
and no one knew the place.
And Clement counted the seventy years of the captivity from the burning until the second year of Darius son of Hystaspes (Ustasp).
And Haggai and Zechariah the prophets bear witness, who said:
"Lord,
how long will You have no mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah,
against which You have been indignant these seventy years?" And Eusebius and Andronicus also consider it thus.
And others [count it] from the third year of Jehoiakim until the nineteenth year of Cyrus.
And Daniel the prophet [counts it] from the thirteenth year of Josiah, that is, from the beginning of the prophecy of Jeremiah.
And Africanus [counts it] from the beginning of Zedekiah.
Now the years of the twenty-three kings down to the burning were five hundred and twenty-five,
and from Adam, four thousand five hundred and sixteen.
[He reigned] twenty-four years after he burned the Temple
and brought to an end the kingdom of the Jews.
For prior to this, he had reigned another nineteen years,
so that all the years of his reign were forty-three.
And after the burning of the Temple {OCR: ܗܲܝܪܠܵܐ for ܗܲܝܟܠܵܐ}, Nebuchadnezzar went up again for a fifth time,
and waged war against Tyre, and constructed a causeway of stones in the sea out to it.
Then the people of Tyre, being terrified, cast everything into the sea and fled in ships;
and they seized Hiram and killed him.
Now he had lived {OCR: ܚ̣ܝܵܐ (ܗܘ݀ܵܐ؟)} five hundred years, throughout the entire period of the kings of Judah.
